THE REQUEST TO SPEAK FORM ON THE KIOSK ASSISTS THE MAYOR IN ENSURING THAT ALL PERSONS WISHING TO ADDRESS THE CITY COUNCIL ARE RECOGNIZED. IT ALSO ENSURES THE ACCURATE IDENTIFICATION OF MEETING PARTICIPANTS IN THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES. YOUR NAME WILL BE CALLED AT THE TIME THE MATTER IS HEARD BY THE CITY COUNCIL. SPEAKERS MAY NOT YIELD THEIR TIME TO OTHER PERSONS.
PLEASE TAKE NOTICE THAT: THE ORDER OF SCHEDULED AGENDA ITEMS BELOW AND/OR THE TIME THEY ARE ACTUALLY HEARD, CONSIDERED AND DECIDED MAY BE MODIFIED BY THE MAYOR OR THE CITY COUNCIL DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING, SO PLEASE STAY ALERT.

ADJOURNMENT-CITY COUNCIL
NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council and Successor Agency meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council and/or Successor Agency meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv. For more information, please contact the City Clerk's office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council/Successor Agency will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council/Successor Agency meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council/Successor Agency meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council/Successor Agency regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk's Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk’s Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us. Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City's system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE

  CALL TO ORDER

  The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council and regular joint meeting with the City of
  Irvine as Successor Agency to the dissolved Irvine Redevelopment Agency was called to
  order at 4:51 p.m. on November 23. 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic
  Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California; Mayor/Chairwoman Khan presiding.

  ROLL CALL

  Present:  Councilmember/Boardmember: Larry Agran
  Councilmember/Boardmember:  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember/Boardmember: Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor/Vice Chairwoman: Tammy Kim
  Mayor/Chairwoman  Farrah N. Khan

  Mayor/Chairwoman Khan provided the current guidelines for face coverings for members
  of the public attending the meeting in person; noted additional opportunities to participate
  in the meeting virtually; and encouraged those providing public comments to be civil,
  polite, and courteous when addressing one another, City staff, and members of the public.

  In addition, Carl Petersen, City Clerk, provided instructions on how to participate in the
  meeting; and noted that the e-comment feature had been extended, which allowed
  members of the public the ability to submit e-comments on all agenda items, which would
  be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the City's website.

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  • A few initiatives the City is working on in alignment with our City's strategic priorities
  include the following:

  o As part of our Quality of Life, the One Irvine program aims to strengthen and
  enhance the quality of life for residents, stimulate property maintenance and
  landscaping improvements, and decrease calls for public safety and code
  enforcement in Irvine neighborhoods. The program began in 2019 with a focus
  on the North El Camino Real community. The City is gearing up to partner with
  residents in other neighborhoods to identify and address local needs.
  Neighborhood Action Plans will be created based on community feedback.

  Prepared by the City Clerk's Office
 City Council Minutes  November 23. 2021

  o As part of the City's Organizational Excellence, Geographic Information
  System maps are available to help the community find the information they are
  looking for. GIS maps are online at cityofirvine.org/gis and can help locate
  everything from parks, bikeways, and childcare to notable development
  projects. Emergency Preparedness, Capital Improvement Projects within
  Irvine, and more.

  o Public Works and Transportation staff is installing Rectangular Rapid Flashing
  Beacons at seven crosswalk locations throughout the City to improve
  pedestrian safety. Yellow rectangular flashing lights on the beacons will
  increase safety by helping to bring attention to pedestrians as they cross the
  street.

  o A Climate Action and Adaptation Plan has been created in an effort to mitigate
  the impacts of climate change. The plan serves as a roadmap for the
  community and our municipal operations. It will provide comparative options to
  realize our emission reduction goals and help evaluate the City's vulnerability
  to climate-related impacts and provide measures that build resilience to current
  and future climate threats.

  o The City of Irvine continues to look at opportunities for renewable energy within
  the City. Solar power, energy storage, and electric vehicle charging are being
  assessed at several facilities. This effort will reduce electricity costs, provide
  resiliency for City operations, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and provide
  clean transportation services to our community.

  • The City will be hosting several events next month to celebrate the City's 50^^
  anniversary. The community is invited to the 50th Anniversary Symposium and
  Photo Exhibition Reception at City Hall on December 7 from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m., to
  celebrate Irvine past and present. The Exhibition will look back at the City's rich
  history with a special oral history video and symposium highlighting how Irvine
  became the model master-planned community it is today. In addition, the winning
  images in the City's 50*'^ Anniversary Photo Contest will be on display. The 24
  contest finalists, including the grand prize winner and individual category winners,
  will be recognized at an opening reception.

  On December 11, a birthday party will be held for the whole community. Families
  and friends are invited to Great Park from 2 to 7 p.m. for a family-friendly evening
  with music and dancing, crafts and interactive activities, food trucks, and some
  special surprises. The community is also invited to join a block party on December
  28 to celebrate the date of the City's incorporation. The largest community centers
  will host mini celebrations for residents from 2 to 5 p.m. with crafts, cupcakes, and
  anniversary photo ops. For more information on each of these events, visit
  cityofirvine.org/50th.

  Prepared by the City Clerk's Office
 City Council Minutes  November 23. 2021

  • The community is invited to celebrate the holidays all winter long in Irvine. Great
  Park has transformed into a winterscape featuring holiday-themed art, music, and
  decorations. Enjoy festive lights, photo ops, and family activities during "Holidayz
  at the Park" through January 2. On Saturday, December 4, celebrate the season
  as "snow" falls over the Irvine Civic Center and the community gathers for the
  annual Holiday Tree Lighting ceremony. The event will be held from 4 to 6:30 p.m.
  and will include visits with Santa Claus, live holiday music, and a winter-themed
  train route. The Irvine Animal Care Center will host its 15th annual Home for the
  Holidays Pet Adoption Fair on Sunday, December 5, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. The
  Home for the Holidays Pet Adoption Fair will be held outdoors at the Irvine Animal
  Care Center and will feature local pet rescue groups and pet-related vendors,
  along with upwards of 200 adoptable animals. Event admission is $5 per person;
  children 13 and younger are free. Advance ticket reservation is required for all
  attendees, including children. Tickets are available at yourirvine.org.

  Use the City's magic online mailbox to send letters to Santa by December 13, and
  get a reply as fast as reindeers fly. Allow one week for responses; classrooms,
  allow two weeks. To submit your letter, visit cityofirvine.org/LettersToSanta. For
  additional  information  on  all  of  these  events  and  more,  visit
  cityofirvine.org/speciale vents.

  • The community is invited to play a role in helping to develop Great Park by visiting
  the Digital Foyer, a virtual space where residents can access information about
  Great Park planning and share feedback. The Digital Foyer has seven stations
  offering information about the Great Park project and opportunities to share input
  about the types of uses and designs residents would like to see at the park. The
  City is excited to offer this public engagement tool in eight additional languages:
  Arabic, Farsi, Japanese, Spanish, Vietnamese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional
  Chinese, and Korean. In addition, the community is invited to the next planning
  and public input Town Hall Meeting on Wednesday, December 1 from 6 to 7:30
  p.m. at Great Park Hangar 244. Visit yourgreatpark.org for more information.

  • Last week, a delegation of Orange County mayors, including Mayor Tiffany Ackley
  (Aliso Viejo); Mayor Connor Traut (Buena Park); Mayor John Stephens (Costa
  Mesa); Mayor Pro Tem Sue Kempf (Laguna Beach); Mayor Freed Minager
  (Laguna Miguel); Mayor Shari Home (Laguna Woods); and Mayor Vicente
  Sarmiento (Santa Ana), joined Mayor Khan at the Irvine Civic Center to celebrate
  the passing of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. This
  landmark legislation, which was signed by President Biden on November 15, will
  help build more equitable, sustainable, and resilient communities, and also provide
  funding for local governments to address a broad range of infrastructure needs. It
  is the City Council's hope that Irvine becomes more resilient than ever by ensuring
  every resident can connect to reliable high-speed internet and by focusing on the
  repair and rebuilding of roads and bridges, with special attention on climate change
  mitigation, specifically meeting the goal of carbon neutrality by 2030.

  Fred Judd, Irvine resident and Investment Advisory Committee Member,
  suggested that the City not invest in entities that manufacture tobacco
  products,firearms, and alcohol; and those who engage in drilling offossil
  fuels. He also encouraged investments in entitles that support the City's
  environmental objectives.

  Prepared by the City Clerk's Office
 City Council Minutes  November 23. 2021

  Hoiyin Ip, Irvine resident, expressed concern related to the lack of
  accessibility to the City's Investment Policy and full investment
  disclosures that the City is involved in.

  City Council discussion included: expressing concern with investing in
  companies that do not align with the City's values; questioned how the
  City could choose better investments that ensured the City's
  environmental goals were met; suggested that the City should not have
  to wait for State guidance to determine which companies to invest in;
  and suggested that investments related to for-profit prisons and military
  industrial complexes also be reviewed.

  Don Collins, City Treasurer, suggested the item be tabled until clearer
  guidelines could be provided by the State and/or Federal government.

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Khan, and seconded by Councilmember
  Agran, to:

  1)  Adopt RESOLUTION NO. 21-70 - A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA,
  ADOPTING THE CITY'S ANNUAL INVESTMENT POLICY
  FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2022
  2)  Direct staff to begin a process to identify any and all
  investments with companies that are countering the City's
  environmental and social objectives.
  3)  Direct staff to begin the process to divest from those entities
  and identify new source of investments that align with the City's
  environmental and social values.

  The motion carried as follows:

  This item was agendized at the request of Mayor Khan and

  intent of the review, and suggested that the Sunshine Ordinance remain
  intact.

  review; suggested that the Sunshine Ordinance remain intact;
  suggested that the process be open and transparent; spoke in support
  of Councilmember Agran serving on the sub-committee; and in
  opposition to the requirement for two councilmembers to agendize
  items.

  Kevin Corrigan, Irvine resident, spoke in opposition of creating a
  subcommittee and repealing the Sunshine Ordinance; and suggested
  that staff return within 60 days to present the best practices from other
  legislative agencies to the City Council.

  the subcommittee, to which Councilmember Kuo declined based on
  current commitments to other boards and committees. Mayor Khan
  expressed an interest in serving on the subcommittee.
